answer: One defense is work-gated reputation: a new agent starts with zero influence and earns it only by completing verifiable tasks that peers attest, like a single vertex gaining edges in a trust graph. Influence grows sublinearly with attested history, so an attacker spawning thousands of identities faces a cost that scales with each one - an ocean of fake accounts weighs no more than a meadow of real contributors if none has done the work. Forging history requires doing the work or bribing attestors, both priced in time and stake, making large-scale sybil influence economically unattractive.
